comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C28-C29 regarding correlation between Myo10 levels and filopodia number. Both find the power law relationship compelling and well-supported by the data.

Perfect agreement on claims C7, C45-C46, C85-C86 regarding minimum Myo10 molecules for filopodia initiation. Both find the live-cell quantification methodology compelling and the measurements valuable for understanding Myo10 action.
Perfect agreement on claims C47-C48, C89 regarding distinct puncta emerging from existing filopodia. Both find the quantification of different filopodial phases compelling and well-documented.

Perfect agreement on claims C94-C96 regarding differential behavior of neighboring filopodia and spatial specificity of regulatory mechanisms. Both find the inferences from live-cell observations compelling.

Strong disagreement on evaluation type for claims C107-C112 regarding the Myo10-fascin dynamics model. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN (speculative, lacks direct validation), while peer reviewers find it SUPPORTED and compelling as a mechanistic model consistent with quantitative findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C3, C30-C35, C68-C69 regarding spatial patterning and periodic distribution. Both find the rose plot analysis and imaging data compelling, with constant Myo10 per filopodium particularly well-documented.

Perfect agreement on claims C8-C9, C50-C53, C92-C93 regarding differential Myo10 accumulation in growing vs. retracting filopodia. Both find the temporal dynamics data and statistical analysis compelling.

Strong disagreement on evaluation type for claims C43-C44, C78-C79 regarding membrane-docked Myo10. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN (speculative, lacks direct evidence), while peer reviewers find it SUPPORTED and accept the calculations without critique.

Perfect agreement on claims C4-C5, C38-C39, C64 regarding log-normal distribution of Myo10 in filopodia. Both find the quantitative measurements and statistical characterization compelling and well-supported.

Perfect agreement on claims C6, C40-C42, C73 regarding excess Myo10 beyond actin binding sites. Both find the evidence compelling, though OpenEval notes assumptions in calculations while peer reviewers acknowledge 'limitations to this study.'

Strong disagreement on evaluation type for claims C19-C21, C102 regarding the overexpression system and filopodia induction. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong methodological support, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to concerns about extrapolation to physiological conditions despite authors' justification.

Agreement on claims C2, C26, C58 regarding quantitative measurements of Myo10 distribution. Both find the evidence compelling, though OpenEval notes C59-C60 are more speculative while peer reviewers group these with supported findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C10, C54, C97 regarding inverse correlation between Myo10 quantity and filopodial speed. Both find the correlation analysis compelling and note its importance for understanding dynamics.
Perfect agreement on claims C55-C57 regarding measured filopodial speeds. Both find the measurements compelling and consistent with prior literature.

Strong disagreement on evaluation type for claims C83-C84, C105 regarding actin fraying as alternative explanation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN (lacks direct evidence in this system), while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and find the mechanistic interpretations compelling.

Strong disagreement on evaluation type for claims C27, C60, C67 regarding autoinhibition and PIP3 speculation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN (explicitly speculative, lacks direct evidence), while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and find the mechanistic speculation compelling.
Perfect agreement on claims C23-C24 regarding HaloTag calibration methodology. Both praise the quantification method as novel, valuable, and providing compelling evidence with appropriate controls.

Partial disagreement on claims C74-C76 regarding lack of shutoff mechanisms and disorderly packing. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with logical conclusions, while peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED but emphasize potential impacts on transport and morphology.

Disagreement on evaluation type for claims C59-C60 regarding autoinhibition and PIP3 limitation. OpenEval rates C59 as reasonable inference but C60 as speculation lacking evidence (overall UNCERTAIN for R15), while peer reviewers rate both as SUPPORTED and compelling.

Disagreement on claim C104 regarding membrane-docked Myo10. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN (speculative, lacks direct evidence), while peer reviewers include it in SUPPORTED findings about crowding and its potential impacts.

Agreement on claim C63 as appropriate citation of prior literature. OpenEval groups it with other literature citations as SUPPORTED context, while peer reviewers specifically praise the methodology as novel and valuable.

OpenEval result R17 addresses background claims C1, C11-C18 as established literature context (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background material.

OpenEval result R14 addresses claims C98-C101 as appropriate citations of prior literature supporting the inverse speed relationship (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific literature citations.

OpenEval result R18 addresses claims C62-C63, C71-C72, C77, C80-C82, C87-C88, C91, C103, C106 as appropriate literature citations (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these literature citations except C63, focusing instead on primary findings.
